Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — we finished a progressive rollout of the Sherpa eviction tuning + INT8 microkernel switch for runtime-core on dedicated clusters. Canary->100% completed over ~3h. Early aggregate results look good: p50 down ~18ms, p95 down ~32ms, p99 down ~60ms in our 512-token text-gen suite, and token compute cost ~-14% on average across our most common workloads. :tada:

deploy-bot: deploy started 2026-03-23T15:12:02Z for runtime-core -> sherpa-evict:v2 (canary 2026-03-23T15:12:02Z)

Josh Patel: Nice. What are the exact runtime flags so infra teams can reproduce on dev clusters?

Maria Chen: Flags we flipped: `runtime.prefetcher.sherpa_evict=true` and `kernel.quant_mode=int8_fast`. Also set `runtime.eviction.window_ms=1200` for the new policy. Example deploy CLI:```
rc deploy set --service runtime-core --image=runtime-core:sherpa-evict-v2 
  --env RUNTIME_FLAGS="runtime.prefetcher.sherpa_evict=true;kernel.quant_mode=int8_fast;runtime.eviction.window_ms=1200"
```

Arjun Rao: Can you share the benchmark harness or the dashboard link? Curious about model-specific variance (Llama2 vs MPT).

Maria Chen: Dashboard is pinned under Console > Rollouts > Sherpa Evict (internal). Quick summary: Llama2 workloads saw ~16% cost reduction, MPT-like models ~11% (higher sparsity in thosenets). We included KV-prefetch hit-rate stratification — hit lift ~7% in typical chat traces.

Laura Kim: Were there any customer-facing changes? Need to coordinate comms if behavior noticeably changes.

Maria Chen: No API surface changes. Behavior: slightly faster tail for multi-turn chat. For Dedicated customers we plan a short heads-up note; email template below.

Maria Chen: Email snippet: "Heads up — we've rolled out a runtime optimization (Sherpa eviction + INT8 path) that reduces inference latency and cost for most workloads. No action required; fallback enabled. Contact support if you see regressions."

Josh Patel: Good. What are the rollback/fallback triggers? Ops wants clear SLOs to watch.

Maria Chen: Rollback protections: automatic fallback to FP16 kernels when QoS triggers hit (p99 latency increase >10% sustained for 5m) or error rate >0.5% for 5m. Rollout policy was 2%->20%->50%->100%. We accelerated after metrics remained stable at the 50% stage for 40min.

ops-bot: ALERT RULES: Fallback will trigger if p99(latency) rises >10% for 5 continuous minutes OR err_rate > 0.5% for 5 continuous minutes.

Arjun Rao: I'll add a short probe job that exercises long-context KV heavy traces to watch eviction interactions. Please tag me on anomalies.

Maria Chen: Thanks — appreciate that. TL;DR: meaningful latency + cost wins with conservative fallback. Rollout id: 0x7c3f. If anyone wants access to the raw bench runs or cost breakdowns, DM me and I'll share the notebook and raw traces.

Josh Patel: :rocket: Great work team. I'll paste a short ops runbook in eng-ops after lunch.

Maria Chen: cheers.
